items.claim: Non-object `next({ctx})` now replaces the whole ctx type, but runtime still spreads it over the previous ctx
items.consequence: Runtime merges ctx as `{ ...callOpts.ctx, ...nextOpts.ctx }` (procedureBuilder.ts:373), so an undefined or non-object ctx passed to next() leaves the previous ctx intact. The new type instead replaces it: `next({ ctx: flag ? { extra: 1 } : undefined })` used to infer `{user} | {extra,user}` and now infers `{extra,user} | undefined`, so `ctx.user.id` fails with 'ctx is possibly undefined'; `next({ctx: undefined})` and `next({ctx: {} as unknown})` are typed `undefined` / `{}` instead of keeping `{user}`. Overwrite<{a:1},{b:2}|undefined> changed from `{a:1}|{a:1,b:2}` to `{a:1,b:2}|undefined` (verified with tsc against the old definition). Impact is limited to unusual next({ctx}) arguments, and the input-side result is the intended fix.
items.proposed_fix: Keep the replace-when-not-both-objects rule for _input_in/_input_out only, and give the _ctx_out / ResolveOptions ctx paths a merge that treats undefined/null/unknown members of TWith as 'keep TType' (runtime spreads them). Alternatively document the ctx behavior change and add a ctx test.

items.claim: Doc comment says a never TWith keeps TType, but every branch returns never; the trailing `: TType` branch is unreachable
items.consequence: `TWith extends any` is distributive and true for every non-never member, so `: TType` at line 29 can never be selected; Overwrite<string, never> and Overwrite<{a:1}, never> both evaluate to never (verified with tsc), contradicting the stated contract of an @internal type that is re-exported from internals.ts. A future reader relying on the comment will get never instead of TType.
items.proposed_fix: Reword the comment to say a never TWith yields never, and drop the dead `: TType` branch (or, if 'keep TType when TWith is never' is intended, gate on `[TWith] extends [never] ? TType : ...` before the distributive checks).

native_payload.intent: Fix Overwrite<TType,TWith> so key-wise overwrite only happens when both sides are objects and otherwise TWith replaces TType, so `.input(z.string()).use(mw)` infers `string` instead of a mangled object type; adds a type-level regression test.

residual_risks: Only packages/tests was type-checked (clean at head); a root-level tsc ran out of memory in the adversarial read, so examples and other packages' type tests were not checked against the new Overwrite.
Overwrite<any, X> now yields a union of X and an index-signature object, and Overwrite<{a:1}, any> yields any; both were already loose and are not judged consequential.
Not assessed: PR body is an empty template and the regression test file is named issue-5020 while the PR is #5017; no plan document was found.
testing_gaps: The regression test covers only a string input through .use() (which does fail against the old Overwrite); it has no assertion for ctx merging through .use()/next({ctx}), object input chained via .input() after .use(), optional-object input with middleware, or Overwrite with never/unknown/any.
voidWithMiddleware is declared in the test router but never asserted on.
The type assertions only run under tsc (expectTypeOf is a no-op at vitest runtime); the tests-package tsc passes at head.

coverage.notes: Focused path: own correctness read plus one independent adversarial read. The cross-model peer was unavailable by run policy, so the adversarial lens ran as a local adversarial-reviewer on the same model family (corroboration only, not cross-model). No other reviewer agents and no validator ran. No CODING_STANDARDS.md/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md governs the changed files (CONTRIBUTING.md is not a criteria file). Compound Packs not applied; learnings, agent-native gaps and deployment notes not assessed. Scope was local (base: merge-base of the PR). tsc on packages/tests passes at head; old-vs-new Overwrite comparisons were run with scratch tsc.
